About.history1: Chilean aquaculture has evolved into a highly competitive, modern, and export-oriented industry, becoming a cornerstone of the national economy. In 2022, Chile ranked 10th in global aquaculture production and was the fifth-largest exporter of aquatic animal products, generating USD 8.5 billion. This success has been primarily driven by salmon and mussel farming, which accounts for approximately 99% of the annual harvest. This high level of specialization has positioned Chile as the world’s second-largest producer of salmon and mussels, behind Norway and China.
About.title2: Despite these remarkable achievements, the growth rate of Chilean aquaculture has slowed
About.text2: And the sector is currently nearing stagnation due to a range of interconnected challenges. Recognizing the importance of aquaculture for the country’s development, CONICYT (now ANID) identified aquaculture as a strategic area in 2011 to strengthen scientific knowledge and promote sustainability, launching a competitive call to establish a center of excellence funded by the Fund for Research Centers in Priority Areas (FONDAP).
About.title3: In this context, INCAR was established in 2012 as Chile’s first Interdisciplinary Center for Aquaculture Research.
historyParagraphs: For more than a decade, INCAR has gained national and international recognition for generating robust scientific knowledge and translating it into practical recommendations for both the public and private sectors.

After 13 years of generating high-quality knowledge and human capital, FONDAP INCAR transitions into the Interdisciplinary Center for Aquaculture Research – Applied Research, CIA INCAR². This new phase will focus on generating knowledge and developing technologies that balance the competitiveness of the aquaculture sector with social well-being and environmental sustainability in Chile.

INCAR² will drive the development of technologies, processes and knowledge that contribute to a more sustainable and competitive aquaculture sector, while also promoting the identification and use of opportunities for productive diversification. Its results will be transferred to the public and private sectors to strengthen the competitiveness of the Chilean economy and contribute to the well-being of society.
About.text4: Our center is made up of nearly 90 people, including researchers, professionals, technicians, and undergraduate and graduate students. INCAR² is structured around eight research lines and develops advanced scientific and technological solutions to address the main challenges of Chilean aquaculture. Its work includes the development of vaccines, tools to reduce the use of antimicrobials, environmental models, and climate resilience strategies, with a strong focus on sustainable solutions, competitiveness, animal welfare, and effective knowledge transfer to the productive sector.
About.institutionsText: In this new stage, the center is led by the University of Concepción as its sponsoring institution, together with Universidad Andrés Bello, Universidad de Talca and Universidad Austral de Chile as associated institutions. The center is funded by the National Agency for Research and Development (ANID), part of Chile’s Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation.
About.missionText: To lead innovation and transfer solutions through world-class scientific and technological research, fostering collaboration and interdisciplinarity to improve the sustainability and competitiveness of Chile's aquaculture industry and support the country's development.
About.visionText: To be a global leader in applied research and innovative solutions, driving the sustainable development of aquaculture and positioning Chile at the forefront of the industry worldwide.
About.objGeneralText: To advance the sustainable development of aquaculture in Chile through world-class interdisciplinary research, innovation, capacity building and collaboration, promoting knowledge transfer, technological progress and global alliances to address the critical challenges of the sector and contribute to social welfare.
objectives: Conduct world-class interdisciplinary and collaborative scientific and technological research, both nationally and internationally, to address the critical challenges of aquaculture in Chile.
Strengthen collaboration between emerging research groups in Chile, promote sustainable aquaculture and accelerate the development of new technological services and products.

Develop and implement innovative solutions to the challenges of the aquaculture sector, contributing to productive diversification through the co-creation of new knowledge, techniques, technologies, products, processes and services that foster the sustainable development of aquaculture.
Effectively disseminate INCAR²'s research results and ideas to specialized audiences and broader sectors of Chilean society, promoting greater awareness and understanding of sustainable aquaculture.

Train and support advanced capabilities for research and technology transfer, facilitating the integration of professionals into the aquaculture sector and strengthening their capacity for innovation.
Build and strengthen national and international collaboration networks in sustainable aquaculture, facilitating the exchange of knowledge, resources and best practices.

Governance.title: Governance
Governance.councilText: The Academic Board will comprise the Center's Principal Investigators and is the leading corporate decision-making body.
Governance.institutionsText: INCAR² was established as a center for applied aquaculture research to address emerging challenges in the sector, providing innovative solutions that strengthen industry sustainability and societal well-being. This effort stems from a strategic alliance led by the Universidad de Concepción as the host institution, together with the Universidad Andrés Bello, Universidad de Talca, and Universidad Austral de Chile as associate institutions. The center is funded by the National Research and Development Agency (ANID), under the Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge, and Innovation of Chile.
Governance.boardText1: The Board of Directors is composed of the Vice-Rectors for Research and Development of the Universidad de Concepción (host institution), Universidad Andrés Bello, Universidad Austral de Chile and Universidad de Talca. The board is completed by the Center's Director and four representatives from non-academic sectors and institutions: INTESAL; AmiChile; SERNAPESCA; and SUBPESCA.
Governance.boardText2: The Center's Director reports to the Board, which provides the strategic guidelines for the Center in order to facilitate and coordinate inter-institutional relations among the four participating universities and to promote a synergistic interaction that strengthens INCAR² science. This Board is to be constituted during the first year of execution.
Governance.alliancesText1: INCAR² Center emerges as an applied aquaculture research hub, designed to address the sector’s new challenges and deliver innovative solutions that strengthen Chile’s competitiveness and promote societal well-being. Its creation is based on a strategic alliance among four leading universities and supported by public institutions, private organizations, and international partners, consolidating a robust and diverse collaboration network.
Governance.alliancesText2: The Center’s ecosystem of strategic partners is composed of the Undersecretariat of Fisheries and Aquaculture (SUBPESCA), the National Fisheries and Aquaculture Service (SERNAPESCA), the National Institute for Small-Scale Fisheries and Aquaculture (INDESPA), the Fisheries Development Institute (IFOP), SalmonChile A.G., the Salmon Council A.G., the Association of Salmon Farmers of Magallanes, the Chilean Mussel Farmers Association (AmiChile A.G.), the Institute of Aquaculture at the University of Stirling, and WWF Chile, as well as domestic and international collaborations.
Governance.advisoryText1: The National Advisory Board is composed of the following members: the Center’s Director, the Vice-Presidents of Research and Development of the associated institutions, and at least two members linked to the productive sector, whether public and/or private. It is envisaged that the members will include the National Deputy Director of Aquaculture of the Chilean National Fisheries and Aquaculture Service (SERNAPESCA); the Head of the Aquaculture Division; the Undersecretariat of Fisheries and Aquaculture of the Ministry of Economy, Government of Chile (SUBPESCA); the Marine Program Officer (Chile) of the World Wildlife Fund (WWF); the Chief Executive Officer of the Chilean Mussel Farmers Association (AMICHILE); the Chief Executive Officer of the Salmon Technology Institute (INTESAL; this institute is the research branch of the Association of the Salmon Farming Industry of Chile, SalmonChile A.G.); the Salmon Council; and the Association of Salmon Farmers of Magallanes.
Governance.advisoryText2: The role of the National Advisory Board is to present INCAR² to key public and private organizations so that the Center’s actions (research, education, training, transfer, and outreach) remain relevant to public and private stakeholders in Chilean aquaculture and ensure our contribution. This Committee will be established during the first year of execution and must meet at least every six months, keeping formal minutes of the topics discussed.

Vaccines.title: New vaccines
Vaccines.lead: Research Line 1 (RL1) of the INCAR² Center focuses on the development of innovative fish vaccines, as a key tool to advance toward more sustainable, efficient and resilient aquaculture.
Vaccines.focusText: Its main contribution lies in integrating frontier biotechnologies to improve disease prevention, reduce antibiotic use and strengthen animal health and welfare in Chilean aquaculture, especially in salmon farming. RL1 responds to critical sector challenges, such as the insufficient protection of current vaccines, the high burden of bacterial and parasitic diseases —notably Piscirickettsia salmonis and the sea louse Caligus rogercresseyi— and the need for more effective and environmentally responsible technological solutions.
objectives: Develop next-generation vaccines based on recombinant proteins and mRNA for relevant aquaculture pathogens.
Implement oral vaccines using Bacillus spore surface antigen display technology (BSSD), reducing the stress associated with vaccination.
Explore immunostimulation strategies through Dodecin-based technologies.
Evaluate vaccine effectiveness through laboratory challenge tests, including an innovative cohabitation–coinfection model that simulates real farming conditions.
Analyze the economic impact of the developed vaccines for the national and international aquaculture industry.
Vaccines.transferText: RL1 has a strong emphasis on technology transfer, with the potential to generate patents, vaccine prototypes and specialized efficacy evaluation services. Its projections include:
transferItems: New vaccines against the main pathogens affecting Chilean salmon farming.
Scalable technological platforms for the industry, with expected advances in technology readiness levels (TRL 6–8).
Immunological monitoring tools based on biomarkers, applicable to both experimental and commercial vaccines.
Vaccines.closingText: With its interdisciplinary approach and international collaborations, RL1 positions the INCAR² Center as a benchmark in aquaculture vaccinology, contributing directly to the sanitary, environmental and economic sustainability of the aquaculture sector.

Diseases.title: Fish Diseases and Antimicrobial Resistance
Diseases.lead: Research Line 2 (RL2) of the INCAR² Center addresses one of the greatest challenges for sustainable aquaculture: the control of infectious fish diseases and the growing antimicrobial resistance (AMR), in a context of climate change, productive intensification and a One Health approach.
Diseases.focusText: Its central contribution is to generate scientific knowledge and technological solutions that reduce dependence on antibiotics, improve animal health and mitigate the environmental and sanitary impacts associated with aquaculture. RL2 is based on INCAR's solid track record in the study of emerging and endemic pathogens of Chilean salmon farming, such as the agents of tenacibaculosis, Aeromonas salmonicida, Piscirickettsia salmonis and others, as well as the comprehensive analysis of the molecular and ecological mechanisms that explain the emergence, persistence and dissemination of AMR in aquatic environments.
objectives: Understand the mechanisms of pathogenicity, virulence and resistance of pathogens relevant to Chilean salmon farming and strengthen the surveillance of emerging diseases.
Develop immunological products and non-pharmacological strategies (functional additives, phages, natural compounds) for the prevention and control of infectious diseases.
Create innovative, rapid and low-cost diagnostic methods, suitable for field use in freshwater and marine farming systems.
Generate experimental and advanced diagnostic services oriented to the productive sector.
Characterize antimicrobial resistance in farmed fish, wild fish and environments associated with aquaculture, identifying resistance genes, mobile genetic elements and susceptibility patterns.
Diseases.transferText: RL2 has a clear orientation toward transferring results to the public and private sector, with concrete applications such as:
transferItems: Multiplex molecular diagnostic platforms for rapid identification of pathogens and variants.
AMR and resistome monitoring tools, including biomarkers that support sanitary decision-making and the responsible rotation of antimicrobial therapies.
New feed additives with immunostimulant and antibacterial potential.
Services for the determination of epidemiological cut-off values (ECOV) and antimicrobial susceptibility evaluation, essential to prevent therapeutic failures.
Diseases.closingText: With an interdisciplinary approach, national and international collaborations and a strong scientific-technological base, RL2 positions INCAR² as a benchmark in aquaculture animal health and antimicrobial resistance management, contributing directly to a more responsible, resilient aquaculture aligned with the principles of sustainability and integral health.

Omics.title: Omics solutions for Aquaculture
Omics.lead: Research Line 3 (RL3) of the INCAR² Center focuses on addressing the major sanitary and environmental challenges of Chilean aquaculture through the integrated use of omics technologies, epigenetics, single-cell transcriptomics, microbiomes, and advanced biotechnological tools.
Omics.focusText: Its core contribution is the generation of applied knowledge and innovative solutions that enhance the health, welfare, and productivity of aquaculture species, while reducing environmental impacts and strengthening the sustainability of the sector. RL3 investigates how environmental factors, pathogens, and host-associated microbiota interact with the genome to modulate phenotype, disease resistance, and productive performance in key species such as Atlantic salmon, the Chilean mussel (Mytilus chilensis), and the sea louse (Caligus rogercresseyi). This integrative approach supports a transition from reactive management to a predictive and precision-based aquaculture framework.
objectives: Induce and characterize early-life epigenetic changes driven by environmental factors to improve robustness and disease resistance.
Develop epigenetic and molecular markers applicable to fish health monitoring and selective breeding programs.
Identify immune and cellular biomarkers of salmon diseases using single-cell transcriptomics.
Detect and validate multi-omic markers of pharmacological resistance in sea lice populations.
Develop microbiome-based therapeutic and nutritional strategies, including pre-, pro-, and postbiotics.
Implement sanitary surveillance and diagnostic tools based on CRISPR-Cas systems.
Omics.transferText: RL3 delivers practical technological solutions for sustainable aquaculture, including:
transferItems: Epigenetic reprogramming protocols during early developmental stages to enhance disease resilience.
Novel genetic and epigenetic markers to strengthen breeding and selection programs.
Advanced diagnostic biomarkers for key pathogens such as Piscirickettsia salmonis, supporting improved vaccine strategies.
Tools for early monitoring of resistance to anti-parasitic treatments, reducing drug use and environmental impact.
Functional diets based on microbiota-derived ingredients to improve fish health and productivity.
Rapid, sensitive, and cost-effective diagnostic methods for aquaculture pathogens using CRISPR-Cas technology.
Omics.closingText: Through strong integration of basic and applied research, RL3 of the INCAR² Center contributes to the development of a more sustainable, innovative, and competitive Chilean aquaculture, aligned with climate change challenges, biosecurity needs, and responsible seafood production.

Welfare.title: Stress and Animal Welfare
Welfare.lead: Research Line 4 (RL4) of the INCAR² Center focuses on understanding how productive and environmental stressors inherent to intensive aquaculture affect fish physiology, welfare, and adaptive capacity, particularly in salmonids.
Welfare.focusText: Its main contribution is the generation of scientific knowledge and technological tools that support improved animal welfare, enhanced resilience to diseases, and optimized productive performance within a sustainable and ethical aquaculture framework. RL4 addresses the effects of multiple simultaneous stressors—such as temperature, oxygen availability, and stocking density—during early developmental stages, integrating physiological, transcriptomic, epigenetic, and microbiome-based approaches. This comprehensive perspective advances understanding of how farming conditions influence key biological processes, including growth, immune responses, metabolism, and long-term adaptive potential.
objectives: Characterize physiological and molecular responses induced by single and multiple stressors in teleost fish.
Evaluate the effects of environmental and epigenetic manipulation on adaptive capacity under productive challenges.
Develop and validate animal welfare indicators, including non-invasive (behavior, body size, environmental conditions) and invasive (physiological and molecular markers) metrics.
Identify welfare-related parameters associated with disease control treatments, ensuring treatment efficacy without compromising fish health.
Analyze responses to key pathogens, such as Infectious Pancreatic Necrosis Virus (IPNV), and to critical processes such as seawater transfer.
Welfare.transferTitle: Technological Applications and Contribution to Sustainable Aquaculture
Welfare.transferText: The outcomes of RL4 will enable the development of practical solutions for Chilean aquaculture, including:
transferItems: Non-invasive methods for monitoring welfare and stress in production systems.
Epigenetic reprogramming protocols to enhance fish responses to diseases and productive stressors.
Tools to predict future performance, including growth, immune competence, and metabolic adaptation.
Welfare protocols during sanitary treatments, supporting responsible and efficient fish health management.
Transfer of standardized welfare indicators to inform decision-making in both public and private sectors.
Welfare.closingText: In this way, RL4 of the INCAR² Center contributes to the advancement of an aquaculture model that integrates productivity, animal welfare, and sustainability, aligned with scientific, regulatory, and societal expectations for responsible aquatic food production.

Ecosystems.title: Aquaculture Impacts on Ecosystems
Ecosystems.lead: Research Line 5 (RL5) of the INCAR² Center addresses the main environmental and ecosystem challenges associated with Chilean aquaculture, with a particular focus on salmon and mussel farming in marine, coastal, and freshwater ecosystems.
Ecosystems.focusText: Its core contribution is the generation of scientific knowledge, indicators, and technological tools that enable the assessment, prediction, and mitigation of environmental impacts, supporting an ecosystem-based and science-driven management of aquaculture. RL5 investigates how aquaculture production influences key processes such as trophic status, organic matter cycling, biodiversity, environmental quality, and the dynamics of harmful algal blooms (HABs), integrating ecological, biogeochemical, oceanographic, and advanced modeling approaches. This comprehensive perspective provides critical support for spatial planning, carrying capacity estimation, and the prevention of environmental and sanitary crises.
objectives: Assess the environmental impacts of aquaculture on marine, coastal, and freshwater ecosystems.
Generate quantitative ecological indicators to support environmental management and sustainability.
Improve understanding of the ecological and biogeochemical drivers of harmful algal blooms and the role of aquaculture in their occurrence.
Develop early warning indicators for disease outbreaks and critical shifts in the epidemiological status of farming areas.
Implement state-of-the-art Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) models and integrated modeling tools to support decision-making.
Contribute to spatial planning and adaptive management of aquaculture in Patagonian ecosystems.
Ecosystems.transferText: Outcomes from RL5 are translated into practical solutions for the public and private sectors, including:
transferItems: Environmental and ecological indicators for assessing the impacts of salmon and mussel farming.
Early warning systems for harmful algal blooms, Caligus rogercresseyi, and diseases such as salmonid rickettsial septicemia (SRS).
CFD models and digital twins of aquaculture facilities for real-time monitoring of oceanographic and hydrodynamic variables.
Tools for carrying capacity estimation and aquaculture spatial planning.
Assessment of seabed restoration technologies and environmental performance.
Development of epidemiological risk maps based on ecological and molecular indicators.
Ecosystems.closingTitleAccent: environmentally responsible, socially accepted and scientifically informed
Ecosystems.closingText: Through these contributions, RL5 of the INCAR² Center plays a key role in advancing an environmentally responsible, socially accepted, and scientifically informed aquaculture, strengthening ecosystem sustainability and the long-term competitiveness of Chilean aquaculture under climate change and increasing environmental demands.

Resilience.title: Increasing Aquaculture Resilience
Resilience.lead: Research Line 6 (RL6) focuses on strengthening the sustainability of Chilean aquaculture by reducing its impacts on marine ecosystems and enhancing its capacity to adapt to climate change.
Resilience.focusText: Despite the rapid early growth of salmon and mussel farming, the sector now faces stagnation due to spatial limitations, regulatory constraints, and increasing environmental pressures. RL6 addresses a critical gap: the lack of ecosystem-scale assessments and accessible tools to evaluate and communicate the real impacts of aquaculture. At the same time, it responds to emerging threats such as harmful algal blooms, rising temperatures, hypoxia, salinity changes, and parasite proliferation, all intensified by climate change.
objectives: Develop a Traffic Light System (TLS) to regulate aquaculture production based on ecosystem carrying capacity and emission thresholds.
Build a dynamic climate risk mapping system integrating environmental, production, socioeconomic, and governance variables.
Design adaptation strategies to reduce risks and create new opportunities under climate change.
Create innovative ecosystem assessment models to evaluate natural and aquaculture-driven variability, particularly in emerging regions like Magallanes.
Resilience.transferText: RL6 delivers cutting-edge tools for sustainable aquaculture management, including:
transferItems: A TLS digital platform and decision-support system to guide production limits and spatial planning.
Climate risk mapping tools for improved site selection and farm management.
Flexible regulatory and farm-siting models that enable adaptive, science-based decision-making.
Production and economic models to optimize efficiency, resilience, and cost-effectiveness.
Benthic biodiversity monitoring systems and ecosystem health indicators.
Climate adaptation plans and governance frameworks fostering public–private collaboration.
Resilience.closingTitle: A resilient and sustainable aquaculture aligned with
Resilience.closingText: Through these innovations, RL6 provides actionable, science-based solutions to improve environmental performance, support regulatory modernization, and promote a resilient and sustainable aquaculture industry aligned with ecosystem conservation.

Interactions.title: Sustainable Interactions between Aquaculture, Fisheries, and Ecosystems
Interactions.lead: Research Line 7 (RL7) focuses on strengthening the integration of aquaculture with artisanal fisheries and coastal ecosystems, promoting sustainable livelihoods and resource recovery.
Interactions.focusText: In Chile, where many coastal communities depend on benthic fisheries managed through TURFs (MEABRs), declining fish stocks have created an urgent need for diversification through small-scale aquaculture (SSA). RL7 highlights the potential of SSA—particularly mussel and seaweed farming—as a low-cost, accessible alternative that balances environmental sustainability, economic development, and social equity. At the same time, it addresses key challenges such as stock depletion, harmful algal blooms (HABs), emerging diseases, and limited seed availability for benthic species.
objectives: Develop and transfer nature-based solutions for restocking and restoring commercially important benthic species.
Generate epidemiological and environmental baseline data to support predictive models in aquaculture systems (e.g., Gracilaria farming).
Assess impacts of marine biotoxins on early life stages of cultured species.
Establish a monitoring system for aquatic genetic resources (AGR) under environmental change.
Optimize and scale up seed production technologies for Red Sea urchin.
Conduct bioeconomic assessments to evaluate large-scale production feasibility.
Interactions.transferText: RL7 delivers applied solutions for sustainable aquaculture and fisheries management, including:
transferItems: Restorative aquaculture and restocking protocols (REGA, CBA/CBF) to recover overexploited resources.
Monitoring systems for HABs, biotoxins, and genetic diversity, supporting early warning and adaptive management.
Predictive models and diagnostic tools for disease outbreaks in seaweed farming.
Innovative seed production technologies, including scaling up sea urchin cultivation and improving survival and growth through optimized systems.
Metabarcoding and genomic tools to understand ecosystem dynamics and species adaptation.
Bioeconomic models to guide investment and decision-making in small-scale aquaculture.
Interactions.closingText: RL7 contributes to the transition toward a more resilient and equitable coastal economy by linking aquaculture with fisheries management and ecosystem restoration. Its innovations support artisanal communities, enhance biodiversity recovery, and enable sustainable, climate-adaptive aquaculture practices.

Socioeconomic.title: Socioeconomic Impacts, Governance, and Market Dynamics
Socioeconomic.lead: Research Line 8 (RL8) focuses on strengthening the sustainability and competitiveness of Chilean aquaculture by integrating socioeconomic analysis, governance innovation, and market intelligence.
Socioeconomic.focusText: While aquaculture is a key global source of affordable, high-quality protein, its long-term development depends on balancing economic growth with social equity, environmental protection, and public trust. RL8 addresses critical challenges such as social perceptions of the industry, regulatory uncertainty, climate-related risks, and the need for better integration of small-scale producers into global value chains. It emphasizes the importance of robust socioeconomic data and governance frameworks to support informed decision-making and sustainable sector development.
objectives: Develop applied solutions to enhance resilience and competitiveness under climate change and external shocks.
Measure the socioeconomic impacts of aquaculture to identify opportunities for inclusive development.
Evaluate regulatory frameworks and governance systems to support effective decision-making.
Promote cost-effective sanitary and production practices that improve animal welfare, food safety, and market positioning.
Socioeconomic.transferText: RL8 delivers innovative tools and approaches that support sustainable aquaculture, including:
transferItems: Data-driven assessment platforms integrating socioeconomic, environmental, and governance indicators.
Policy evaluation and decision-support tools for regulatory design and coastal planning.
Economic and bioeconomic models to assess costs, benefits, and incentives (e.g., reducing antimicrobial use).
Early warning systems for health and epidemiological risks, linked to production and market performance.
Market intelligence tools analyzing certification, product demand, and export competitiveness.
Participatory and digital platforms for stakeholder engagement, data visualization, and knowledge transfer.
Socioeconomic.closingText: RL8 strengthens aquaculture governance and market integration by generating evidence-based solutions that improve transparency, efficiency, and sustainability. Its contributions support better public policies, more resilient coastal economies, and stronger positioning of Chilean aquaculture in global markets.

Communications.title: Dissemination and Outreach Program
Communications.lead: INCAR²'s Dissemination pillar is designed to strategically transfer scientific knowledge of excellence toward an ecosystem of experts, decision-makers and aquaculture sector leaders, both nationally and internationally.
Communications.disseminationText: Through the development of political-technical positioning documents, the organization of specialized gatherings and active participation in global innovation platforms, the center seeks to positively influence regulatory frameworks and promote technological solutions that address critical industry gaps, advancing concretely toward aquaculture sustainability. In this way, it ensures that high-impact research translates into concrete tools for regulatory development and the strengthening of inter- and transdisciplinary scientific collaboration networks.
Communications.outreachText: The Social Outreach pillar aims to connect science with citizens, generating a real impact on educational communities, local governments and aquaculture stakeholders (from large and small industry). The strategic plan addresses mass outreach through interactive digital channels, the strengthening of technical-professional education and the promotion of the consumption of marine and aquaculture resources. It also incorporates key support in technology transfer to enable and promote the transformation of the center's innovations into applicable solutions for the socio-productive sector. This builds a solid bridge that empowers communities, drives diversification and ensures the appreciation of knowledge in the territories.

ResearchIndex.title: Research Lines
ResearchIndex.lead: Eight research lines that integrate science, innovation and technology to generate high-impact knowledge and sustainable solutions for the aquaculture sector.

Initiatives.title: Initiatives
Initiatives.caligusText: The research developed by the Interdisciplinary Center for Aquaculture Research (INCAR) in Caligus Rogercresseyi has advanced significantly in the comprehensive understanding of this ectoparasite through a multi-omic and translational approach. From the sequencing of its genome and transcriptomic analysis at different stages of the life cycle, key genes associated with processes such as infestation, reproduction and adaptation to the host have been identified. These studies have made it possible to elucidate molecular mechanisms of resistance to antiparasitics, including structural variations such as CNVs and SNPs in genes related to the cuticle and oxidative stress, which explains multi-resistance phenomena observed in the field. At the same time, INCAR has integrated this information with microbiome studies, life cycle biology and epidemiology, generating a robust basis for the development of applied tools such as diagnostic biomarkers, recombinant vaccines and new therapeutic strategies, including nanoformulations. Together, this approach has driven a paradigm shift towards a more precise and sustainable control of calligidosis in salmon farming, based on molecular knowledge and validation in real productive conditions.
Initiatives.srsText1: The INCAR² Center will direct an important part of its scientific-technological program toward addressing two of the main health challenges in salmon farming: Salmonid Rickettsial Septicemia (SRS) and Tenacibaculosis, referred to as the SRS and Tenacibaculosis Initiative. In this context, it will focus its efforts on developing comprehensive solutions that enable progress toward more effective and sustainable control of these diseases, while also contributing to a better definition of health management strategies.
Initiatives.srsText2: Among its main lines of action is the generation of technological innovations aimed at new, more effective vaccines, as well as the search for alternatives to the use of antimicrobials, such as functional feeds, therapies based on plant-derived compounds, and the use of phages. Likewise, the center will promote the development of rapid, low-cost diagnostic kits that facilitate timely detection and immediate response at the cage level, thereby strengthening control capacity under real production conditions.

Collaborations.title: National and International Collaboration
Collaborations.lead: INCAR²'s mission is to drive innovation and transfer solutions through world-class scientific and technological research, fostering collaboration and interdisciplinarity to strengthen the sustainability and competitiveness of Chile's aquaculture industry. Given the complexity of these challenges, national and international collaboration is a key pillar of our strategy, generating both measurable benefits—such as increased scientific impact and access to funding—and qualitative outcomes by expanding research horizons.
Collaborations.nationalText: At the national level, INCAR² collaborates with leading institutions including COPAS Coastal Center, CIEP, the Patagonia Institute, Patagonia Biotech Hub, Aquabench, IFOP, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Valparaíso, University of Chile, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile, and Universidad de O'Higgins.
Collaborations.internationalText: INCAR²'s international network officially includes the following institutions: the Aquaculture Institute (University of Santiago de Compostela, Spain); the Friedrich-Loeffler-Institute (Federal Research Institute for Animal Health, Südufer, Germany); Monterrey Bay Aquarium (USA); the Global Sustainable Aquaculture Advancement Partnership (GSAAP); the UN's Food and Agriculture Organization; Dr. Steven Roberts from the School of Aquatic and Fishery Sciences of University of Washington (Seattle-USA); The Institute of Marine Research (IIM-CSIC-Spain); University of Cadiz (Spain); the Environment for Development (EfD) Initiative, University of Gothenburg (Sweden); Dr. Marilyn Roberts from the University of Washington (USA); Prof. Peter Smith from University of Galway (Ireland); Dr. Carlos Pereira Dopazo from Aquatic One Health Research Center-University of Santiago de Compostela - ARCUS-USC - (Spain); Dr. Simon MacKenzie from the University of Stirling (UK); Collaborations.ecosText: A key milestone is the ECOS-ANID project “Understanding the Effects of Climate Change on Shellfish Aquaculture through Hologenomics (BivalOMICS)”, which supports researcher and student mobility and highlights INCAR²'s capacity to secure international funding.
Collaborations.internshipsText: Additionally, INCAR² fosters internships and collaborative initiatives focused on applied technological development, engaging researchers, students, and stakeholders.
Collaborations.natihText1: INCAR² maintains a strategic collaboration with the National Aquaculture Technology and Innovation Hub (NATIH) at the University of Stirling (UK), supported by a £17 million investment. This partnership provides access to cutting-edge laboratories and infrastructure, strengthening applied research, technology transfer, and human capital development.
Collaborations.natihText2: Together, INCAR² and NATIH promote innovative solutions for sustainable aquaculture, contributing to global economic development and food security. This collaboration includes scientific fellowships, technical training, and technological tours for researchers, students, and the transfer team (INCAR² Acceleration Hub – INAH).

PublicPolicy.title: Public Policy
PublicPolicy.heroTitle: Science, Technology Transfer and Public Policy: INCAR² Policy Briefs
PublicPolicy.intro1: At INCAR² we promote interdisciplinary research across our 8 research lines in order to comprehensively address the complex challenges of sustainable aquaculture development. In this new stage, applied science and technology transfer take on a leading role in turning scientific knowledge into concrete solutions with real impact on the territory and its productive sectors.
PublicPolicy.intro2: So that this frontier scientific knowledge effectively informs decision-making, we created our “Science-based recommendations for public policy”, or INCAR² Policy Briefs. Through this effort we turn our main research milestones and high-impact scientific publications into brief, objective and easy-to-read summaries, designed specifically to connect scientific evidence and technology transfer with policy formulation and strategic decision-making.
PublicPolicy.whyTitle: Why communicate science and transfer technology to decision-makers?
PublicPolicy.whyLead: Our Policy Briefs are aimed at key stakeholders in the public sector, the private sector, NGOs and organised communities, seeking to generate tangible impact along three strategic axes:
PublicPolicy.axis1Title: Improving the quality of public policy
PublicPolicy.axis1Text: Incorporating scientific knowledge and technology transfer into regulatory processes optimises the use of resources and gives greater social and technical legitimacy to the regulations adopted.
PublicPolicy.axis2Title: Managing health and environmental risks comprehensively
PublicPolicy.axis2Text: Decisions based on robust scientific evidence make it possible to mitigate and reduce negative impacts on ecosystems, strengthening the resilience and biosecurity of the aquaculture production system.
PublicPolicy.axis3Text: We position applied science as a strategic and indispensable tool for driving continuous improvement, technological innovation and the sustainable development of aquaculture at local and global scale.
PublicPolicy.listTitle: We invite you to review our Policy Briefs
PublicPolicy.advisoryTitle: Parliamentary Advisory Reports from the Library of the National Congress (BCN)
PublicPolicy.advisoryIntro1: As part of its commitment to generating and transferring knowledge for public decision-making, researchers at the INCAR² Center collaborate with the Library of the National Congress (BCN) in preparing Parliamentary Advisory Reports — technical documents developed to support the legislative, representative and oversight functions of the Senate and the Chamber of Deputies of Chile.
PublicPolicy.advisoryIntro2: These publications are grounded in the principles that guide the BCN's institutional work: equal access, validity, reliability and political neutrality, providing scientific evidence and specialised analysis on issues of strategic interest for the country.
PublicPolicy.advisoryIntro3: The documents are recognised as recommended reading for researchers, aquaculture professionals and decision-makers interested in advancing the development of sustainable aquaculture. We invite you to review those published to date.
PublicPolicy.otherIntro1: In addition to its scientific and technical output, INCAR² promotes and takes part in preparing analysis documents and proposals aimed at contributing to the sustainable development of aquaculture and the conservation of marine ecosystems. These publications bring together scientific evidence, interdisciplinary knowledge and the collaboration of public, private and civil-society actors, with the purpose of providing inputs for decision-making and the design of evidence-based policy.
PublicPolicy.otherIntro2: This section brings together special documents, technical reports and other publications that reflect INCAR²'s commitment to generating applied knowledge and its contribution to the environmental, social and productive challenges linked to marine ecosystems and aquaculture.

Transfer.title: Technology Transfer
Transfer.missionText1: The mission of the Interdisciplinary Center for Aquaculture Research – Applied Research, CIA-INCAR², is to drive innovation and transfer solutions through world-class scientific and technological research, fostering collaboration and interdisciplinarity to improve the sustainability and competitiveness of the aquaculture industry in Chile and support the country's development.
Transfer.missionText2: The complexity of these topics and INCAR²'s interdisciplinary perspective create a unique field for collaboration with emerging research groups in Chile focused on aquaculture, technologies, and innovation. Supporting emerging research groups is a crucial part of our center's strategy, offering significant benefits such as greater technological impact, potential access to new funding sources and markets, opportunities to complement human resources, and the incubation of new businesses such as aquaculture spin-offs and startups. As a result, INCAR² will strengthen its collaborative links, creating a hub of interdisciplinary excellence in aquaculture research in Chile. The following sections present the plan to enhance collaboration among emerging research groups in science and technology.
Transfer.sferaFull: Support Framework for Emergent Research Groups
Transfer.sferaText: SFERA is a program for emerging research groups (ERGs) in aquaculture that face resource and networking barriers. It offers direct funding, access to INCAR² infrastructure, training, and networking opportunities with public and private stakeholders.
Transfer.inahText1: INAH is the driving force behind the center's technology transfer, facilitating the flow of scientific advancements to industry and public agencies. It will focus on networking, intellectual property, business plans, and collaborative events.
Transfer.inahText2: Its primary function is to bridge the gap between scientific research and industrial application, facilitating the maturation, validation, and scaling of technologies developed by researchers associated with the center.
Transfer.inahText3: INAH will operate as a hub for convergence between science, industry, and entrepreneurship, integrating research capabilities, scientific infrastructure, specialized knowledge, and stakeholders from the productive sector.
Transfer.synergyText1: The SFERA – INAH will promote the generation of new technologies and knowledge, designed to strengthen national Emerging Research Groups (ERGs), facilitate their consolidation, and accelerate the development of innovative solutions relevant to the Chilean aquaculture industry.
Transfer.synergyText2: The SFERA initiative will work jointly with the INCAR² Acceleration Hub (INAH) to promote scientific and technological innovation in aquaculture. INAH will act as a driving force to foster collaboration among emerging research groups in Chile.
Transfer.objGeneralText: To support the scientific and technological advancement of national emerging research groups external to the Center, with the aim of developing science, technology, and innovative solutions in aquaculture.
objectives: Promote collaboration between INCAR² members and ERGs in areas aligned with the Center's objectives.
Provide financial support for scientific and technological research activities of ERGs through collaborative projects with INCAR².
Accelerate technology readiness levels (TRLs) by facilitating access to INCAR²'s infrastructure and specialized equipment.
Support the training and development of human capital within ERGs in areas related to INCAR²'s expertise.
Facilitate networking and collaboration between ERGs and stakeholders from the public and private sectors.
Transfer.contactText: Contact us and turn your knowledge into real-world solutions.

Events.title: Events
Events.intro1: Events CIA-INCAR² is a space dedicated to the dissemination of congresses, seminars, workshops, launches, calls for proposals and scientific events linked to aquaculture and applied research.
Events.intro2: Here we share opportunities for meeting, knowledge exchange and collaboration between academia, the productive sector and decision-makers, highlighting initiatives oriented toward innovation, sustainability and the development of aquaculture from an interdisciplinary perspective.
Events.intro3: Follow us and stay up to date with the main milestones, events and activities driven by INCAR², connecting science, technology and impact for the aquaculture sector.
Events.srsText1: SRS 2026 is the first International Conference aimed at advancing the fight against piscirickettsiosis and its bacterial agents, to be held in the city of Puerto Varas, Chile, on 9 and 11 November 2026.
Events.srsText2: The aim of the meeting is to create a space for interdisciplinary exchange that allows presenting and discussing the most recent advances in the study of piscirickettsiosis, as well as disseminating new findings, innovative technologies and applied solutions for its control.
Events.srsText3: The program will be structured into four thematic modules, designed to promote, through science and technology, the development of strategies that strengthen the health and sustainability of salmon farming globally.
Events.srsText4: The participation of researchers, industry professionals, regulatory and health authorities, as well as representatives of civil society interested in addressing one of the most relevant diseases affecting salmon farming, is expected.
Events.srsText5: Likewise, the program will include spaces oriented toward fostering critical analysis and networking among participants, addressing key aspects such as diagnosis, epidemiology, therapeutic strategies and the environmental and socioeconomic impact of this disease.
Events.epimarText1: Welcome to the Fourth International Symposium on Epigenetics in Marine and Aquatic Research (EPIMAR 2027), set to take place in Puerto Varas, Chile, from May 25 to 28, 2027.
Events.epimarText2: EPIMAR first took place in Montpellier, France, in October 2020. Despite being held online due to the pandemic, it attracted participants from across the globe, highlighting the immense interest in the field. This was followed by successful editions in Woods Hole, USA (2022) and Barcelona, Spain (2025). Now it's time for Chile.
Events.epimarText3: EPIMAR 2027 will bring together a global community of scientists exploring epigenetic and epigenomic mechanisms that influence the biology, adaptation, and evolution of marine organisms. Our goal is to foster interdisciplinary dialogue across marine biology, genomics, aquaculture, and environmental sciences.
Events.epimarDates: Abstract submissions open: October 15, 2026 · Abstract deadline: January 4, 2027 · Early bird registration until March 15, 2027 · Symposium: May 25–28, 2027, Puerto Varas, Chile.
